The honest part

What got you here won't get you there.

You climbed the first mountain. The company, the exit, the numbers that once felt like the whole point. By any outside measure, it worked.

And yet, in the quieter moments, a question keeps coming back. What now? What is all of this actually for?

Most people in your position try to answer that alone, inside their own heads. It rarely works. The drive and self-reliance that took you up the first mountain won't take you up the second.

Saying that out loud isn't a defeat. It's a relief. It shows you what you may have been optimising your life around, and lets you choose again.

Nobody regrets the bets that failed. They regret the ones they never placed. Jed Shamel
Who it's for

For the second mountain leader.

Founders and CEOs who have had real career and financial success, and are now, often privately, asking what comes next.

  • You've built something, or sold something, and arriving didn't feel the way you thought it would.
  • You're respected and capable, and you're still carrying the big questions on your own.
  • You want the next ten years to be shaped on purpose: your health, your wealth, your relationships.
  • You have little patience for performance, theatre, or being sold to.

The question the week puts to you: who are you as a second mountain leader, and who are you becoming over the next ten years?

What the retreat is

A room where it can be said honestly.

Seven men, one villa, one question. The retreat replaces isolation with a room of people in the same position, who can be straight with one another. Jed facilitates, and the room rests on three things.

Candour

Radical honesty in the room. Nobody hides.

Confidentiality

What's said here stays here. That's what makes the honesty safe.

A shared commitment

Everyone is there to define their second mountain, and the bet they'll place on it.

Three lenses for the work

Look honestly at what you regret, what you envy, and what you want to build next.

Regret

What you would do differently, and what that tells you about what matters now.

Envy

What you quietly envy in others, read as an honest signal rather than a weakness.

Compound Leadership

Jed's framework for bringing health, wealth and relationships into one system, so the change compounds over years, not weeks.

The place

M Villa Comporta

A five-star villa in the pine forest with a 25m pool, a mile and a half from Praia do Carvalhal. Surf, paddleboard and yoga are built into the week.

You have your own suite, and a door that closes. Somewhere to step away between sessions, to sit with what comes up, and to sleep before the next day. The work goes deep. This is where you come back to yourself.

The month after

The four days are not the product. What you do in the four weeks afterwards is.

  1. Last morning

    Your one page

    You write down the bet you're placing. Jed keeps a copy.

  2. Week 1

    The reconvene

    The seven of you back together for 90 minutes. You read your page out. This is where relapse gets caught.

  3. Week 3

    One-to-one with Jed

    60 minutes on your page and nothing else.

  4. Weeks 1 to 4

    The group thread

    A live line to the six other men, and to Jed by voice note, for the month.
